steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Ferrous metals contain iron - magnetic, prone to rust (except stainless). Mild steel: low carbon, ductile, weldable. Stainless steel: chromium content prevents corrosion - cutlery, medical instruments. | Key Fact: Cast iron: high carbon (2-4%), excellent compressive strength, self-lubricating - engine blocks, manhole covers. | Key Fact: Aluminium: lightweight (1/3 steel's density), corrosion-resistant (oxide layer), excellent conductor - aircraft, cans, window frames. | Key Fact: Copper: excellent electrical and thermal conductor, ductile, malleable, antimicrobial - wiring, plumbing, PCBs.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain why stainless steel is used for surgical instruments whereas mild steel is not, despite both being ferrous metals. | Justify the use of aluminium rather than steel for aircraft fuselage construction. | A product designer needs a gold-coloured, corrosion-resistant material for a door handle. Compare brass and gold-anodised aluminium.
